mainTopic: The defeat of the צדוקים on a son's daughter's inheritance, teachings about leaving a son or a student behind, three teachings of רבי פנחס בן חמא, and the grandfather-versus-uncle question.
overview: This amud opens at the end of a debate with the צדוקים. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי breaks their קל וחומר: a son's daughter has a stronger right than a daughter, because she inherits even alongside brothers. The חכמים win, and the day becomes a festival. A פסוק about שבט בנימין is read as a one-time exception in which a son's daughter did not inherit. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that God is angry at one who leaves no son. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי then argue over whether 'those with no replacements' means one with no son or one with no student, and the גמרא works out who said which view. Three teachings of רבי פנחס בן חמא follow: דוד 'slept' because he left a son as great as himself, poverty is harder than fifty plagues, and a חכם should be asked to pray for the sick. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that a father comes before his descendants. It uses this rule to answer רמי בר חמא's question of whether a grandfather or an uncle inherits first, and then starts asking why he needed to ask at all, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Breaking the צדוקי's argument
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rejects the צדוקי's קל וחומר. A son's daughter has a stronger right than a daughter, so you cannot learn the daughter's case from hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is our perfect Torah not worth at least as much as your empty chatter? A son's daughter is special, because she has strong rights even when there are brothers. Would you say the same about a daughter, who has weak rights when there are brothers?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers the צדוקי by showing that his קל וחומר does not work. The son's daughter and the daughter are not equal in strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקי argued: if a son's daughter inherits, a daughter surely should, since she is a closer relative. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי points out a big difference. A son's daughter takes her dead father's share even next to his brothers, but a daughter gets nothing at all when there are sons. Since the son's daughter is actually the stronger one, the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: His son's daughter (granddaughter through a son)
Her power is strengthened, her right is stronger
Her power is weakened, her right is weaker

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think closer family always means a stronger right to inherit. Here the granddaughter (through a son) beats the daughter, because she takes her father's place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard example of breaking a קל וחומר with 'מה ל...': you find a strength in the source case that the new case does not have.

phrases.english: Shall our perfect Torah not be
phrases.notes: He means: isn't our Torah worth at least as much as your empty talk? The word 'worth' is understood.

phrases.english: like your idle chatter?
What about his son's daughter?
Her power is strengthened
where there are brothers.
phrases.notes: She inherits her dead father's share right alongside her father's brothers.

phrases.english: Would you say the same about his daughter,
whose power is weakened
where there are brothers?
phrases.notes: A daughter gets nothing from her father when he has sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְבַת בְּנוֹ שֶׁכֵּן יִפָּה כֹּחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the צדוקי's קל וחומר from the previous part of the daf.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole קל וחומר from a son's daughter to a daughter.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source case (son's daughter) has a strength the new case (daughter) does not have: she inherits even next to brothers.

steps.title: The חכמים win and make the day a festival
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים defeated the צדוקים, and that day was set as a festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: They defeated them, and they made that day into a festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story. The חכמים won the debate, and the day was celebrated as a יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדוקים had no answer to רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's point, so the הלכה stayed like the חכמים: a daughter does not inherit together with a son's daughter. The festival marks this victory for the Oral Torah's reading.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is like the חכמים: a son's daughter inherits her father's share, and a daughter does not share with her. The צדוקים' קל וחומר was rejected.

phrases.english: And they defeated them,
phrases.notes: The חכמים won the argument against the צדוקים.

phrases.english: and that day they made into a festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִצְּחוּם וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם עֲשָׂאוּהוּ יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the result of the rejection in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים' view was upheld, and the day became a festival.

steps.title: A special arrangement for שבט בנימין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the survivors of שבט בנימין. רבי יצחק says it teaches that a son's daughter would not inherit with the brothers in that tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they said: the inheritance of the survivors belongs to בנימין, so that a tribe not be wiped out from ישראל.' רבי יצחק of the house of רבי אמי said: this teaches that they made a condition for שבט בנימין that a son's daughter would not inherit together with the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying on the topic of a son's daughter, the גמרא brings a פסוק from שופטים. רבי יצחק explains it as a one-time rule for שבט בנימין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a son's daughter inherits her father's share, as we just saw. For שבט בנימין they made an exception, so that the land would stay with the few surviving men. This does not cancel the normal rule. It is a special arrangement to save the tribe.

keyTerms.meaning: A tribe should not be wiped out
It teaches (introduces a lesson from a פסוק)
That they stipulated or made a condition

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a change to the general law. It was an exception only for שבט בנימין at that time.

phrases.english: 'And they said: the inheritance of the survivors is for Benjamin,'
phrases.notes: שופטים 21:17

phrases.english: 'so that a tribe not be wiped out from Israel.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak of the house of Rabbi Ami said:
This teaches that they made a condition for the tribe of Benjamin

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תִּירַשׁ בַּת הַבֵּן עִם הָאַחִין
phrases.english: that a son's daughter should not inherit together with the brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִתְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching about a son's daughter's inheritance, showing a special exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שבט בנימין they made a condition that a son's daughter would not inherit along with the brothers.

steps.title: God is angry at one who leaves no son
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: God is filled with anger toward someone who leaves no son to inherit him. This is learned from the shared word root of 'והעברתם' and 'עברה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: anyone who does not leave a son to inherit him, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is filled with anger toward him. It says here 'and you shall pass on (והעברתם) his inheritance', and it says there 'That day is a day of anger (עברה)'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement about inheritance. A man with no son is a target of God's anger, and this is proven from a word link between two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the inheritance section, when a man has no son, the Torah uses the word 'והעברתם' for passing his property to his daughter. That word shares a root with 'עברה', anger, in צפניה. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי links the two through a גזירה שוה: when the inheritance must be 'passed' away from a son, it hints at divine anger.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves a son to inherit him
Is filled with anger toward him
It is written here, and it is written there (sets up a word link between פסוקים)
And you shall pass on (the inheritance)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a גזירה שוה can be used for a lesson about values and not only for practical הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
Anyone who does not leave a son to inherit him,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָלֵא עָלָיו עֶבְרָה
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, is filled with anger toward him.
It is written here: 'and you shall pass on his inheritance',
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:8

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'That day is a day of anger.'
phrases.notes: צפניה 1:15. Both words share the root letters ע-ב-ר, and that is the link.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ בֵּן לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related statement about a man with no son inheriting him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God is filled with anger toward one who leaves no son to inherit him, learned through a גזירה שוה between 'והעברתם' and 'עברה'.

steps.title: A dispute over who has 'no replacements'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי explain the פסוק 'those that have no replacements.' One says it means someone who leaves no son. The other says it means someone who leaves no student.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the פסוק 'Those who have no replacements, and do not fear God,' רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One says: this is anyone who does not leave a son. The other says: this is anyone who does not leave a student.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק that connects to the theme of leaving no son behind. It shows that two אמוראים explain it in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חליפות means 'replacements': someone who carries on after a person is gone. One opinion says a son is the true replacement. The other says a student who carries on your Torah is the true replacement. The גמרא does not yet say which אמורא holds which view, and the next steps try to work that out.

keyTerms.meaning: Replacements: people who take your place after you are gone
One says... and one says: a dispute where we are not told who said which view

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'חד אמר... וחד אמר' does NOT tell you who said what. Do not assume the first name goes with the first opinion. The rest of the סוגיא is about figuring that out.

phrases.english: "Those who have no replacements
phrases.notes: תהלים 55:20

phrases.english: and do not fear God":

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi [disagree].

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ בֵּן.
phrases.english: One says: anyone who does not leave a son.

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ תַּלְמִיד.
phrases.english: And one says: anyone who does not leave a student.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ בֵּן. וְחַד אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַנִּיחַ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of step 4 (anger at one who leaves no son) with a new פסוק that is explained in two ways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'No replacements' means either one who leaves no son or one who leaves no student. The view is not yet assigned to either אמורא.

steps.title: A first guess: רבי יוחנן says 'student'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן is the one who says 'student.' Since all ten of his sons died, he would not say that a man without sons is under God's anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: It may be concluded that רבי יוחנן is the one who says 'student.' For רבי יוחנן said: 'This is the bone of my tenth son.' So we can conclude that רבי יוחנן is the one who says 'student.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out who holds which view. It uses a known fact about רבי יוחנן's life as evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן outlived all ten of his sons, so he himself left no son. It seems unlikely that he would say a man without sons is someone who 'does not fear God.' So the גמרא guesses that he must hold the 'student' view.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be concluded: the גמרא proposes a conclusion based on evidence
My son (short for 'my son' in Aramaic)

phrases.english: It may be concluded that it is Rabbi Yoḥanan who says "student,"
for Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
This is the bone of my tenth son.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן said this when comforting mourners, after all ten of his sons had died.

phrases.english: It may be concluded that it is Rabbi Yoḥanan who says "student."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to assign the two unnamed opinions of step 5 to the right אמוראים.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds the 'no student' explanation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own life: he lost all ten sons and showed the bone of his tenth son to mourners.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יהושע בן לוי could not hold the 'son' view
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוחנן says 'student,' then רבי יהושע בן לוי must say 'son.' But רבי יהושע בן לוי only went to houses of mourning where the person died without sons, based on a פסוק. That practice does not fit with the 'son' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since רבי יוחנן says 'student,' does רבי יהושע בן לוי say 'son'?! But רבי יהושע בן לוי would not go to a house of mourning except to the house of someone who died without sons. As it is written: 'Weep greatly for the one who goes,' and רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this means the one who goes without a male child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא follows its first guess to its result: רבי יהושע בן לוי would then hold the 'son' view. It then challenges that result using a known practice of רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי gave special attention to comforting mourners of people who died without sons, because the פסוק says such a death deserves great weeping. Someone who treats such a person with that much care does not seem to view him as under God's anger. So רבי יהושע בן לוי probably does not hold the 'son' view, and the first guess falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely...: a common opening for a challenge
For the one who goes (away from this world)

steps.confusionAlert: The '?!' on the first line is not a real question. It sets up the challenge that comes right after it: 'Can it really be that רבי יהושע בן לוי says son? Look at what he did!'

phrases.english: And since Rabbi Yoḥanan says "student,"

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר בֵּן?!
phrases.english: does Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say "son"?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לָא אָזֵיל לְבֵי טַמְיָא
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would not go to a house of mourning

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְבֵי מַאן דְּשָׁכֵיב בְּלָא בְּנֵי,
phrases.english: except to the house of one who died without sons,
as it is written: "Weep greatly for the one who goes,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 22:10

phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
[This means] for the one who goes without a male child!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לָא אָזֵיל לְבֵי טַמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the result of step 6's guess and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The result of step 6: that רבי יהושע בן לוי holds the 'no son' explanation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי specially comforted mourners of men who died without sons, treating their deaths as worthy of great weeping. That does not fit with saying God is angry at such men.

steps.title: Answer: רבי יהושע בן לוי says 'student'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips its earlier guess. רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who says 'student,' which leaves the 'son' view for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהושע בן לוי is the one who says 'student.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question by reversing its first guess.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the challenge in step 7, the 'student' view now belongs to רבי יהושע בן לוי. That means the proof from רבי יוחנן's sons in step 6 is set aside. רבי יוחנן ends up holding the 'son' view, even though he himself left no sons.
steps.whatToRemember: Assignment so far: רבי יהושע בן לוי says 'no replacements' means one who leaves no student, which leaves the 'son' view for רבי יוחנן. The guess from רבי יוחנן's life was overturned by רבי יהושע בן לוי's practice. Steps 9–10 then deal with the problem this creates for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
is the one who says "student."
phrases.notes: So the 'son' view now belongs to רבי יוחנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הוּא דְּאָמַר תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 7 and reverses the assignment proposed in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains 'no replacements' as one who leaves no student, and רבי יוחנן explains it as one who leaves no son.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהושע בן לוי says 'student,' רבי יוחנן must be the one who says 'son.' That clashes with רבי יוחנן's own attitude about losing his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since it is רבי יהושע בן לוי who says 'student,' does that mean רבי יוחנן says 'son'?! Then there is a contradiction between one statement of רבי יוחנן and another statement of רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the result of its last conclusion: רבי יוחנן now holds the 'son' view. It then points out that this contradicts what we know about רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, the 'student' view was given to רבי יהושע בן לוי, so the 'son' view falls to רבי יוחנן. But step 6 showed that רבי יוחנן, whose ten sons died, would not say that a man without sons is under God's anger. So the problem from step 6 comes back, now as a contradiction inside רבי יוחנן's own words.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning the switch it made in step 8. It accepts the switch and then shows that the switch causes a new problem for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And since Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
is the one who says 'student' –
does Rabbi Yochanan then say 'son'?!
There is a contradiction between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yochanan!
phrases.notes: The other 'רבי יוחנן' is his attitude from step 6: all ten of his sons died, so he wouldn't say a sonless man is under God's anger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the step 8 conclusion and shows that it creates a contradiction.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man whose own ten sons died would not say that a man who leaves no son is under God's anger. Yet that is now the view given to him.

steps.title: One view is his own, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. One statement is רבי יוחנן's own view, and the 'son' teaching is his teacher's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the two statements between two people: רבי יוחנן himself and his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'son' teaching is one רבי יוחנן passed on in his teacher's name. Step 4 showed him quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחאי about a man who leaves no son. His personal view, shaped by his own life, is different. Repeating a teacher's teaching does not mean it is his own opinion.
steps.whatToRemember: The final setup is this: רבי יהושע בן לוי says 'student.' The 'son' view is passed on by רבי יוחנן in his teacher's name, while his own view is different.

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
this one is his own,
that one is his teacher's.
phrases.notes: His teacher here is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, whom he quoted in step 4 about the man who leaves no son.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דִידֵיהּ, הָא דְרַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two statements between two people (his own view and his teacher's)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements are רבי יוחנן's own opinions, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'son' teaching belongs to his teacher; רבי יוחנן's own view is different.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next three teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short memory aid for three upcoming teachings: הדד, a poor person, and a wise person.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: הדד, a poor person, and a wise person.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives three key words to help you remember the order of the teachings that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one teaching that follows. 'הדד' is the first, and it starts right away in the next step. The other two come in steps 16 and 17.

phrases.english: (Memory aid: Hadad, a poor person, and a wise person.)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section after the son/student discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for the three teachings that follow.

steps.title: Why does דוד 'sleep' but יואב 'die'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן חמא asks why one פסוק uses 'sleeping' for דוד's death but 'dying' for יואב's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פנחס בן חמא taught: What does it mean when it is written, 'And הדד heard in מצרים that דוד slept with his fathers, and that יואב the captain of the army was dead'? Why is 'sleeping' said about דוד, while 'death' is said about יואב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן חמא points to one פסוק that describes two deaths in two different ways, and he asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men had died, yet the same פסוק says דוד 'slept' and יואב 'died.' Such a clear difference in wording calls for an explanation. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught a deeper explanation of a פסוק
What does it mean when it is written

phrases.english: Rabbi Pinchas ben Chama taught,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"And Hadad heard in Egypt
phrases.notes: מלכים א 11:21

phrases.english: that David slept with his fathers,
and that Joab the captain of the army was dead"?
For what reason, about David,
is 'sleeping' said about him,
while about Joab, 'death' is said about him?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן חָמָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first teaching ('Hadad') from the memory aid in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק calls David's death 'sleeping' but Joab's death 'dying.'

steps.title: Leaving a son makes death like sleep
steps.stepSummary: דוד left a son, so the פסוק speaks of him 'sleeping.' יואב left no son, so it speaks of him 'dying.'
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד, who left a son, has 'sleeping' said about him. יואב, who did not leave a son, has 'death' said about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פנחס בן חמא answers his own question: what makes the difference is whether the man left a son behind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who leaves a son is described as only 'sleeping,' because his line goes on through his son. A man with no son is described as fully 'dead.' This fits the earlier theme of the page: leaving a son behind matters a great deal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching supports the earlier 'son' view: leaving a son behind gives a person a kind of continuation after death.

phrases.english: David, who left a son –
'sleeping' is said about him.
Joab, who did not leave a son –
'death' is said about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּוִד, שֶׁהִנִּיחַ בֵּן – נֶאֶמְרָה בּוֹ שְׁכִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference in wording reflects whether the man left a son: David did and is said to 'sleep'; Joab did not and is said to 'die.'

steps.title: But יואב did have a son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the last answer: a פסוק in עזרא mentions descendants of יואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did יואב really leave no son? But a פסוק says: 'Of the sons of יואב: עבדיה son of יחיאל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 13 by quoting a פסוק that shows יואב had descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 explained 'dying' by saying יואב left no son. If יואב had sons, as the פסוק in עזרא shows, that explanation seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: And Joab did not leave a son?!
But isn't it written: "Of the sons of Joab: Obadiah son of Jehiel"!
phrases.notes: עזרא 8:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יואב left no son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in עזרא lists 'sons of יואב,' so he did leave descendants.

steps.title: A son as great as himself
steps.stepSummary: The answer is refined: דוד left a son as great as himself, and יואב did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, דוד, who left a son like himself, is described as 'sleeping.' יואב, who did not leave a son like himself, is described as 'dying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer so it fits the פסוק about יואב's descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not whether there was a son at all, but whether the son was 'כמותו,' equal to his father. דוד's son was great like him, so דוד is described as only 'sleeping.' יואב's descendants were not on his level.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who leaves a child as great as himself is described as 'sleeping,' as if he had not truly died.

phrases.english: Rather: David, who left a son like himself,
"sleeping" was said about him.
Joab, who did not leave a son like himself,
"dying" was said about him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by refining step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יואב had no son at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: יואב had sons, but none as great as himself.

steps.title: Poverty is harder than fifty plagues
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן חמא teaches from איוב that poverty at home is worse than many plagues.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פנחס בן חמא taught: Poverty in a person's home is harder than fifty plagues. איוב cried out that God's hand had struck him, and his friends told him that he had chosen this suffering over poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching from the memory aid in step 11, the 'poor person.' רבי פנחס proves from איוב that poverty is worse than plagues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב suffered terrible plagues, yet his friends said 'you chose this rather than poverty.' That means that, between the two, poverty is the harder suffering.

phrases.english: Rabbi Pinchas ben Chama taught:

phrases.aramaic: קָשָׁה עֲנִיּוּת בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Poverty in a person's home is harder
than fifty plagues,
as it says: "Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends,
for the hand of God has touched me,"
phrases.notes: איוב 19:21

phrases.english: and his friends were saying to him:
"Be careful, do not turn to wrongdoing,
for you chose this over poverty."
phrases.notes: איוב 36:21. 'This' is איוב's suffering, which was chosen as easier than poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second item in the memory aid from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Poverty at home is harder than fifty plagues.

steps.title: Ask a wise person to pray for the sick
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בר חמא teaches that someone with a sick person at home should ask a חכם to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פנחס בר חמא taught: Anyone who has a sick person at home should go to a חכם and ask him to pray for mercy, as the פסוק says: 'The anger of a king is like messengers of death, but a wise man will calm it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching from the memory aid, the 'wise person.' A sick person's family should ask a חכם to pray for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the King's anger to messengers of death and says a wise man can calm it. רבי פנחס reads this to mean that a חכם's prayer can turn away the danger of illness.

keyTerms.meaning: will calm it, will make up for it

phrases.english: Rabbi Pinchas bar Chama taught:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חוֹלֶה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone who has a sick person in his home
should go to a wise man
and he will ask for mercy for him,
as it says: "The anger of a king is messengers of death,
but a wise man will calm it."
phrases.notes: משלי 16:14

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last item of the memory aid from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone with a sick person at home should ask a חכם to pray for him.
steps.whatToRemember: The three teachings of the memory aid: הדד (a son like his father), a poor person (poverty), and a wise person (prayer for the sick).

steps.title: The משנה's general rule of inheritance order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: whoever comes first in inheritance, his descendants also come first, and a father comes before all his descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: whoever comes first in inheritance, his descendants also come first. And a father comes before all of his descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side teachings and quotes the משנה's general rule. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two parts. A relative's place in line passes to his descendants, and a father comes before his own descendants. The second part will be used to answer רמי בר חמא.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
Anyone who comes first in inheritance,
his descendants come first,
phrases.notes: Literally 'those who come out of his thigh,' meaning his children and their children.

phrases.english: and the father comes before all his descendants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side teachings and returns to the משנה's laws of inheritance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Descendants take their ancestor's place in line, and a father comes before his descendants.

steps.title: Grandfather or uncle: who inherits first
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether the father's father or the father's brother inherits first, using the example of אברהם and ישמעאל inheriting עשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: the father's father and the father's brother, like אברהם and ישמעאל inheriting עשו's property, which of them comes first?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא asks a real question about the order of inheritance between a grandfather and an uncle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עשו's father יצחק has died. אברהם is עשו's grandfather, and ישמעאל is יצחק's brother, so he is עשו's uncle. Both are related to עשו through יצחק, so who has the stronger claim?

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
The father's father and the father's brother,
such as Abraham and Ishmael with Esau's property,
phrases.notes: אברהם is עשו's grandfather, and ישמעאל is his uncle, the brother of his father יצחק.

phrases.english: which of them comes first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a case under the rule just quoted from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a grandfather or an uncle inherits first.

steps.title: רבא: the father comes before his descendants
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the משנה: a father comes before all his descendants, so אברהם comes before ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: the father comes before all his descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רמי בר חמא's question by pointing to the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישמעאל is אברהם's son, one of his descendants. The משנה says a father comes before his descendants, so the grandfather, אברהם, inherits before the uncle, ישמעאל.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
The father comes before all his descendants.
phrases.notes: This is the line from the משנה quoted in step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 using the משנה from step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The grandfather comes first, because a father comes before his descendants, and the uncle is his descendant.

steps.title: Why did Rami bar Chama need to ask
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask why רמי בר חמא had a question when the משנה seems to answer it clearly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר חמא? (Why did he ask, if the משנה already says this?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge: how could רמי בר חמא ask something the משנה already answers? The rest of this challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the answer is right there in the משנה, a scholar like רמי בר חמא would surely know it. So his question must be about something the משנה does not settle, and the גמרא is about to explain what.

keyTerms.meaning: and רמי בר חמא? (why did he ask?)

phrases.english: And Rami bar Chama?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the dilemma of step 19 could exist, given רבא's answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's question in step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly says a father comes before his descendants, so there seems to be nothing to ask.
